chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
To fulfill the need of a believer is better than providing one thousand horses in the way of Allah, and freeing one thousand slaves.
He also said: If any believer goes out to help his brother in a need, Allah writes for him a good deed for every step, erases from him a sin, and elevates him a degree.
And any believer who relieves his fellow believer of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress in the hereafter.
And if any believer comes to the aid of one who is oppressed, that would be better than fasting for a whole month and performing i'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque.

key_terms.قَضَاءُ حَاجَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: Fulfilling the need of a believer

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a fellow believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the practical service of fulfilling a believer's needs above major acts of worship, equating it to freeing a thousand slaves or the merit of a thousand horses in jihad. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on social solidarity, where every step taken to assist a brother earns a good deed, erases a sin, and raises one's spiritual rank. Furthermore, relieving a fellow believer's distress is portrayed as a direct means of securing relief from the trials of the Hereafter, surpassing even the reward of a month of fasting and seclusion in the Sacred Mosque.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 111. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
To fulfill the need of a believer is better than providing one thousand horses in the way of Allah and freeing one thousand slaves.
He also said: If any believer goes out to help his brother, Allah writes for him a good deed for every step (he takes) and erases from him a sin and elevates him a degree.
And any believer who relieves his fellow believer of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress in the hereafter.
And if any believer comes to the aid of one who is oppressed, that would be better than fasting for a whole month and performing i'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque (in Makkah).
